post.description: Fetch styles for records that have none yet. Runs as a job (Discogs allows 60 calls a minute).
Delete every download no track still needs (kept: analysis waiting for you, or never analysed).

get.description: How much audio the app has downloaded and still keeps (never your own files).

post.description:
Find audio for every record that has not been searched yet, one after the other. Records already
searched are skipped, so running it again only continues where it stopped. BPM and key are not touched.

Find every track not searched yet on YouTube, record by record (links only, no quota used). Running it
again only continues where it stopped.
Reveal the Dataview examples file in Finder (macOS only; elsewhere just report the path).

get.description: The numeric id Bandcamp's embed player needs (it is only on the page).
The sources the audio search can use, grouped as Settings shows them.

delete.description: Drop a second (or later) copy. Copy 1 is the record itself: delete the record instead.

get.description:
The shelf: units, their cubes and sections with the records in each, and the unsorted
records with a suggested section.

post.description: Add a divider: a new section at the right end of the cube.

put.description: Put records in a section, or back in unsorted with section_id null.

delete.description: Remove a divider; its records merge into the neighbouring section.
Its records go back to unsorted.

get.description: What differs between the library and the Discogs collection. Changes nothing.

delete.description: Let imports bring a release you once deleted here back again.

post.description: Import the Discogs collection records missing here; wishlist ones become owned.
Add exactly these owned records to the Discogs collection (the ones the preview listed).
Release details and tracklists again from Discogs, keeping everything you added.
Back up, delete every owned record and its data, then import the Discogs collection.
Put exactly these wishlist records on the Discogs wantlist (the ones the preview listed).
Take exactly these owned records off the Discogs wantlist.
Save the look under a name; an existing preset with that name is replaced.

Look a release up and describe it as a label. Nothing is stored; a record already in the
library brings its BPM, key, tags and notes along.
Draw a label that belongs to no record. Nothing is stored.

get.description: Records that moved from the wishlist to owned, newest first (the last 90 days, at most 20).

delete.description:
Delete the record with its tracks, notes and tag links. An owned record that is in the Discogs
collection leaves it too with from_discogs; otherwise it stays there and imports skip it.

post.description:
Analyse the whole record, or only `track_ids` when given, from audio that is already there: your own
files, then what the audio search found. 409 when none of those tracks has audio yet.

get.description: What audioresearch found for each track, and which link each track plays.

post.description: One more copy of the record, unsorted unless a section is given.
Drop analysis proposals (all of them, or only `track_ids`) without touching the tracks.

Search this record's audio from scratch; tracks covered by your own files are left alone. Fast or
lengthy, and which sources, come from Settings. BPM and key are not touched.
Find this record's tracks on YouTube (again, with `refresh`). Links only, nothing is downloaded.

get.description: The label as the database describes it: the starting point for the editor.

post.description: Draw the (possibly edited) label. Nothing is stored: edits apply to this print only.

Put one of your own files in the record's audio folder (the request body is the file) and match it
to its track by its name. Nothing is searched; your file becomes that track's audio.
Save the chosen tracks' analysis proposals onto them. Only records you own can be validated.

get.description:
Each track's YouTube video, found or not, including the YouTube links the audio search already found;
tracks with neither are left out.
Notes with a highlighted snippet, plus records whose artist, title or label match.
Every style in the library with its record count, for filter and editor pickers.
Your own file for a track, for the player: only files level 0 matched, inside AUDIO_DIR.

post.description:
Start the Google sign-in: open the returned page; Google comes back to the callback, which returns to
Settings on the page that asked (this app, or the dev server).

delete.description: Forget the client ID and secret saved in Settings, and sign out.

put.description:
Keep your own Google app's client ID and secret (your own 10,000 units a day), checked with Google
first. A different app than before signs you out of YouTube.

get.description: Your playlists, to pick where tracks go.

post.description:
Add these tracks' videos to one of your playlists, in the order given. A video already in it is
skipped, so adding twice is safe. Each video added costs 50 of YouTube's 10,000 daily quota units.
